q: In an atom the negatively charged electrons are moving around a ____ charged nucleus.
e: In an atom the negatively charged electrons are moving around a positively charged nucleus. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: Some of these electrons are near the nucleus while other electrons are further ____ from the nucleus.
e: Some of these electrons are near the nucleus while other electrons are further away from the nucleus. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: Since positive and negative charges attract each other, electrons experience an ____ force of the nucleus.
e: Since positive and negative charges attract each other, electrons experience an attractive force of the nucleus. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: As the attractive force is greater for the electrons closer to the nucleus so these electrons cannot move ____.
e: As the attractive force is greater for the electrons closer to the nucleus so these electrons cannot move freely. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: The electrons closer to the nucleus are called ____ electrons.
e: The electrons closer to the nucleus are called bound electrons. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: The electrons far away from the nucleus (or) the outer electrons experience less attractive force of the ____.
e: The electrons far away from the nucleus (or) the outer electrons experience less attractive force of the nucleus. Nucleus here means the tiny positive core of an atom, protons and neutrons. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons.

q: This means that the outer electrons are loosely bound and are called ____ electrons.
e: This means that the outer electrons are loosely bound and are called free electrons. Free names this means that the outer electrons are loosely bound and.

q: They can move from one ____ to another.
e: They can move from one atom to another. The physics in this sentence is built around atom.

q: The number of free electrons in a substance depends upon the ____ of that substance.
e: The number of free electrons in a substance depends upon the nature of that substance. The physics in this sentence is built around nature.

q: The substance which has plenty of free electrons is called a ____ and the substance which has very few (or) no free electrons is called an insulator.
e: The substance which has plenty of free electrons is called a conductor and the substance which has very few (or) no free electrons is called an insulator. Conductor here means a material with plenty of free electrons. A conductor has plenty of free electrons, so charge can move.

q: Metals are good electrical ____.
e: Metals are good electrical conductors. A conductor has plenty of free electrons, so charge can move.

q: Some of their electrons are so loosely held to their atoms that they can pass ____ from atom to atom.
e: Some of their electrons are so loosely held to their atoms that they can pass freely from atom to atom. The physics in this sentence is built around freely.

q: Most non-metals conduct electricity poorly or not at all, although ____ is an exception.
e: Most non-metals conduct electricity poorly or not at all, although carbon is an exception. The physics in this sentence is built around carbon.

q: In insulators all the electrons are held tightly in position and unable to move from atom to ____.
e: In insulators all the electrons are held tightly in position and unable to move from atom to atom. An insulator has almost no free electrons, so charge stays put.

q: Insulators are materials that hardly conduct ____.
e: Insulators are materials that hardly conduct electricity. An insulator has almost no free electrons, so charge stays put.

q: Although the electrons are not free to move in insulators, they can be ____ from one object to another.
e: Although the electrons are not free to move in insulators, they can be transferred from one object to another. An insulator has almost no free electrons, so charge stays put.

q: Some substances which contain a moderate amount of free electrons are called ____.
e: Some substances which contain a moderate amount of free electrons are called semiconductors. A semiconductor sits between a conductor and an insulator.

q: Such substances are neither conductors nor ____.
e: Such substances are neither conductors nor insulators. A conductor has plenty of free electrons, so charge can move. An insulator has almost no free electrons, so charge stays put.

q: Silicon and ____ are widely used as semiconductors.
e: Silicon and germanium are widely used as semiconductors. A semiconductor sits between a conductor and an insulator.

q: Metals such as gold, silver, copper, brass, aluminium etc., are good ____.
e: Metals such as gold, silver, copper, brass, aluminium etc., are good conductors. A conductor has plenty of free electrons, so charge can move.

q: Non-metals such as plastic, glass, rubber, wax, quartz, etc., are ____.
e: Non-metals such as plastic, glass, rubber, wax, quartz, etc., are insulators. An insulator has almost no free electrons, so charge stays put.

q: Transistors and other electronic components are made from ____.
e: Transistors and other electronic components are made from semiconductors. A semiconductor sits between a conductor and an insulator.
